bennu.name: Bennu (asteroid)

sunDistance_1e6km.source: Spec: Destinations table (~168, approx.); JPL SBDB gives a = 1.12639 au = 168.5 × 10⁶ km

orbitPeriod_days.source: Spec: Destinations table (~437, approx.); JPL SBDB gives 436.65 d

gm_km3s2.source: JPL Small-Body Database (Chesley et al. 2020, JGR Planets 125, e06363); spec: negligible

radius_km.source: Spec: Destinations table (~0.25, approx.); JPL SBDB diameter 0.48444 km

notes: Gravity assists (flybys) are not modelled. The real OSIRIS-REx used an Earth flyby in September 2017; the game flies a direct transfer instead.
Bennu's gravity is negligible, so the rendezvous Δv is the arrival speed v∞.

nasa-earth-flyby.label: NASA real route (Earth flyby)
nasa-earth-flyby.description: OSIRIS-REx's flown route: launch, a one-year Earth-to-Earth loop with a deep-space manoeuvre, an Earth gravity assist, then a second leg to Bennu. The flyby itself is not simulated; launch C3 is the published value and only the post-flyby leg is computed.

launchDate.source: Lauretta et al. 2017, OSIRIS-REx mission description (arXiv 1702.06981): launched 7:05 p.m. EDT, Sept. 8, 2016

launchC3_km2s2.source: Lauretta et al. 2017 (arXiv 1702.06981): hyperbolic injection C3 = 29.29678 km²/s²

dsmDate.source: Lauretta et al. 2017 (arXiv 1702.06981): large Deep Space Maneuver on Dec. 28, 2016

dsmDeltaV_ms.source: Game estimate: DSM-1 size not given in the paper (NASA mission updates reported ~431 m/s); to verify

flybyDate.source: Earth gravity assist after a one-year Earth-to-Earth loop (paper); exact day Sept. 22, 2017 to verify

approachStartDate.source: Lauretta et al. 2017 (arXiv 1702.06981): beginning of Approach Phase on Aug. 13, 2018

arrivalDate.source: Arrival at Bennu Dec. 3, 2018 (paper gives 'November 2018 rendezvous'); to verify against a NASA source
